title: Name label is set on successful mix; DFU sets it only on recipe fill
claim: DFU's MixCauldron never touches nameLabel (cs:311-360); the label is written only by AddRecipeToCauldron ('nameLabel.Text = recipeName', cs:307) and cleared by every add/remove. The port inverts this: _mix sets this.nameLabel = result.recipe.name on success (potionMakerWindow.js:158) while _fillFrom leaves it blank (finding on :184 above). potionmakerwindow.test.js:136 pins the port's mix-time label.
consequence: The bottom-left name label shows the potion name after mixing (it stays blank in DFU) and stays blank after a recipe fill (where DFU shows the recipe name).

title: Potion maker gold label wired to coins only, not GetGoldAmount
claim: DFU's potion maker label reads GameManager.Instance.PlayerEntity.GetGoldAmount() (cs:138), which is goldPieces + letters of credit (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). The host hands the window 'gold: () => goldAmount(playerEntity)' (worldModes.js:1741) - the coin purse only (court.js:151-152) - which potionMakerWindow.js:246 prints.
consequence: The gold figure in the potion maker understates a player's wealth when part of it is letters of credit (display only - no purchase rides it).

title: Sort-by-cost applies the lycanthropy free-cast quirk; DFU sorts by real cost
claim: DFU's SortSpellsPointCost orders by the raw CalculateTotalEffectCosts spell-point cost (DaggerfallEntity.cs:743-748) with no tag check - the lycanthropy 0-display quirk lives only in PopulateSpellsList (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:264-267). The port's confirmSort cost map uses spellPointCost(sp, castCost) (spellbookWindow.js:511), which returns 0 for the lycanthropy tag (:212-215), so that spell sorts to the front instead of to its true-cost position.
consequence: For a lycanthrope, the second (cost) sort pass places the lycanthropy spell first in the book rather than where its real casting cost puts it in DFU.

title: Spellbook scroll bar is drawn but not interactive
claim: DFU's VerticalScrollBar supports thumb dragging (Update, cs:104-128) and click-above/below-thumb paging by displayUnits (MouseClick, cs:140-148), wired to the list via OnScroll (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:371, :794-797). The port draws the thumb (spellbookWindow.js:784-789) but click() (:649-705) has no branch for SPELLBOOK_RECTS.scrollBar - a click there falls through to 'return true' with no effect, and there is no drag path.
consequence: With more than 16 spells, clicking or dragging the scroll bar does nothing; only the wheel and arrow buttons scroll, where DFU also pages and drags.

title: Spell maker ignores allowedTargets/allowedElements restrictions from chosen effects
claim: DFU restricts target and element to what the chosen effects allow: SetSpellTarget returns early when '(allowedTargets & targetType) == TargetTypes.None' (cs:499-501), SetSpellElement likewise (cs:527-530), and UpdateAllowedButtons recomputes allowedTargets as the INTERSECTION of each effect's Properties.AllowedTargets and allowedElements as magic-only union (cs:563-601), forcing the selection back to the first allowed value. The port's _inputMain cycles rangeType and element freely through all five values (spellMakerWindow.js:187-190) and no allowedTargets/allowedElements state exists anywhere in src/ (grep confirms).
consequence: The port will price and inscribe combinations DFU forbids - e.g. an 'Area at Range' spell from a caster-only effect - producing spells with wrong target semantics and costs that classic/DFU can never mint.

title: envAttack skips Receive(Attack) on doors; DFU fires the door's action record before bashing
claim: DFU WeaponEnvDamage (WeaponManager.cs:460-464) calls action.Receive(player, Attack) on ANY hit object with a DaggerfallAction - including an action door (one GameObject, both components) - and THEN (:467-471) calls actionDoor.AttemptBash(true). Port envAttack (weaponRig.js:159-162): a door branch does attemptBash and returns; only non-doors get receive('Attack'). So an Attack/MultiTrigger-flagged door record (Castle Wayrest doors are MultiTrigger, DaggerfallActionDoor.cs:263 comment) never fires on a weapon hit; the bash path's _execOwnAction passes only the 'Door' trigger, which those flags reject. test/weaponrig.test.js:83 pins the port's behavior, restating the port.
consequence: Attacking an Attack/MultiTrigger action door (e.g. Castle Wayrest DoorText doors whose record runs the trespass check) never fires its record in the port; DFU fires it on every weapon hit.
